requirements.section: 0.3 Kill the Bridge god credential (audit C1)
evidence: D1 migration 0048 and bridge-credentials.server.ts store SHA-256 hashes with per-installation labels, last-use timestamps, rotation versions, and revocation. Legacy conversion is atomic and idempotent; a bounded scheduled backfill includes offline installations.

BridgeInstallationSettings rendered tests verify one-time display, rotation overlap copy, single-click revoke, and removal of late secrets after workspace changes. bridge-installations.test.ts verifies permission checks before every operation.

Commit 31e32e6 moves Desktop, Bridge Desktop, and standalone Bridge keys into OS credential stores and removes plaintext from JSON, native log output, setup HTML, and setup status. Six shared Rust vault tests and 71 standalone Bridge tests pass using isolated fixture stores.

2026-11-04 macOS ARM64: real OS Keychain probe passed native save/read/rotation/deletion/legacy conversion (6 fixture unit tests plus 1 opt-in system test). Standalone Bridge probe passed persistence across a second process, rotation, and cleanup. Random fixture entries only; no existing credentials were read or changed. The manual unsigned build matrix now runs these probes on Windows, Linux Secret Service, Intel Mac, and ARM Mac before bundling.

2026-11-04: unsigned run 41965318862 completed successfully on Windows, Linux, Intel Mac, and ARM Mac. Each job passed real native and standalone OS credential-store round trips and produced Desktop and Bridge bundles. https://github.com/reydisse/showpilot/actions/runs/41965318862

2026-11-04: smoke-bridge-credentials.mjs passed against a disposable built Worker, real Chromium settings UI, real D1, and the standalone Bridge WebSocket library. It verifies one-time key creation and SHA-256 storage, attributed writes, live rotation overlap, immediate refusal of revoked socket writes, rejected reconnects with both key versions, transport-only permissions, rejected query keys, independent installations, and secret removal after reload.

A minimal Worker also reproduces Miniflare delaying the TCP close event after exchanged Close frames. The rehearsal checks immediate write refusal separately and then requires the correct 4403 close event within the standard client close deadline. This is not evidence of instant TCP teardown in production.

Rollout remains separate: migration 0048 and these app changes have not been deployed. Legacy shared keys become hash-only transport credentials through the migration/backfill path; operators must issue distinct labeled keys for computers that previously shared one key. Phase 0 acceptance is verified against isolated fixtures, not by modifying a real organization.

requirements.section: 0.3 Kill the Bridge god credential (audit C1)
evidence: bridge-credentials.worker.test.ts verifies correct-org header authentication and rejection of key query aliases, including valid-header plus query cases. bridge-gateway-security.test.ts verifies all five query aliases are rejected before forwarding.

Standalone Bridge removes legacy key aliases from transport and saved URLs. bridge.test.ts covers each alias; setup-server.test.ts verifies stored URLs and local responses contain no fixture credential.

requirements.section: 0.3 Kill the Bridge god credential (audit C1)
evidence: server.ts no longer derives any member permissions from a Bridge key. Only role=bridge on the Bridge transport endpoint accepts an installation credential; browser device sockets require a member session.
bridge-gateway-security.test.ts rejects key-only rundown, timecode, and lower-third commands and client-role Bridge sockets, and verifies forged auth claims are replaced with server-derived identity.

requirements.section: 0.3 Kill the Bridge god credential (audit C1)
evidence: BridgeRelay revalidates and records the credential ID before forwarding accepted incoming messages, member commands, or internal device dispatches. Audits omit payloads and key values, and record a member actor when present.

Store tests cover per-write audit, monotonic last-used time, stale authority, and org isolation. Real Worker tests verify socket attachments contain only credential identity, operator attribution, rejected writes after revocation, and identity recovery after hibernation.

requirements.section: 0.3 Kill the Bridge god credential (audit C1)
evidence: Rotation keeps old credentials valid for at most ten minutes. Repeated rotations never extend an older overlap. A DO alarm disconnects an idle expired credential; one-click revocation invalidates every version immediately.
Real D1/DO tests cover connected rotation without interruption, revoke/rotate races, idle alarm expiry, and revocation after hibernation. The final targeted BridgeRelay run passed 13 tests.

requirements.section: 0.4 Gate public show state behind a display pass (audit H6)

display-access.worker, display-session, display-gateway-security, DisplayAccessGate, and display-relay-expiry.worker tests verify signature, scope, expiry, revocation checks at entry, limited read projections, and no post-expiry broadcasts after Durable Object hibernation.

2026-11-04: smoke-display-access.mjs ran the production build in local Wrangler with disposable D1 and real Chromium. Signed timer and overlay links rendered, URL passes were removed, HttpOnly cookie access survived reload, and unsigned/wrong-org/wrong-surface/expired links were denied. Full web checks passed: 1248 unit and 115 Worker tests, typecheck, production build.

requirements.section: 0.4 Gate public show state behind a display pass (audit H6)

requirements.section: 0.5 Unguarded destructive actions (audit C12, H3; UI review 9 note; UI/L5)
evidence: Timeline reset/delete, rundown item deletion, and saved-template deletion now use ConfirmDialog. Template failure feedback and reset guards have rendered tests; complete page browser verification remains pending.

Actual Worker tests prove atomic current-item deletion, persistence through eviction, D1 restoration, preservation of later edits, no automatic playback restart, no client-forged restore fields, and invalidation after clear-all.
Shared restoreRundownItem tests cover insertion relative to surviving rows, concurrent edits and duplicate prevention.

2026-11-04: smoke-show-day-safety.mjs passed against the built Worker, real D1, real member login, and Chromium. requirements.section: 0.5 Unguarded destructive actions (audit C12, H3; UI review 9 note; UI/L5)
evidence: Load Demo Show is in the empty timeline body, hidden once any event exists or the clock is running, and disabled while its load is pending. The demo is submitted as one atomic replacement group with requireEmpty/requireStopped/expectedFormat preconditions.

Real Worker test proves no demo is inserted into a running empty timeline or a populated timeline, and the same request succeeds after the clock is stopped and the timeline is empty. Server preconditions prevent a cross-operator race from injecting demo cues into a real timeline.

requirements.section: 0.9 Disconnect honesty on operator screens (UI review 1, 2, 3; live findings)
evidence: Rundown renders a persistent offline/pending count banner and disables transport until matching relay hydration. useRundownSync expires transport after 5 seconds on dispatch and navigation; relay HTTP/WS expiry preserves duplicate acknowledgement and revision arbitration.

Regression tests reproduced the previous eager-connected and stale handoff behavior. Hook and real Worker tests cover stale reconnect, durable edit retention, fresh handoff IDs/deadlines with clock skew, expired HTTP/WS rejection, and applied retry deduplication.
Full web tests passed: 1183 unit and 90 Worker, plus migration/client boundaries. Typecheck and production build passed (174372 gzip bytes). Browser disconnect rehearsal remains pending.

Follow-up: expired transport notices survive successful queued-edit acknowledgements. Production dashboard transport is also disabled offline, and open end-show confirmations remain visible but disabled during a disconnect. Latest validation: 1185 unit / 91 Worker tests, typecheck and production build passed; browser rehearsal remains pending.

2026-11-04: real-browser rehearsal stopped the local Worker process while rundown and timecode tabs were open. Rundown displayed Offline, 0 changes queued and disabled Start/Next; a disconnected Shift+Space did not start after the Worker restarted from persisted state.

requirements.section: 0.9 Disconnect honesty on operator screens (UI review 1, 2, 3; live findings)
evidence: useTimecode reports sent/failed command transport, exposes errors, waits for matching write-session hydration, and starts local sources only after master-status grant plus running-state echo. Disconnect stops sources and pending starts; reconnect does not replay a start. MIDI permission completion after disconnect cannot activate a source.

Event and group saves remain pending until matching IDs arrive in events-update. Timeout/disconnect rejects without clearing the form. Event editor retains a stable retry ID; relay duplicates echo the canonical timeline instead of creating another event. Controls, editor and loader are disabled offline.

New regressions first failed against the original hook (offline local start, pre-grant start, immediate save completion), then passed. Hook/component tests cover grant denial, timeout, disconnection, late MIDI permission, matching group echoes, editor draft retention/retry and exact confirmation.

Validation: full web suite passed (1202 unit tests, 94 Worker tests, migration/client boundaries); typecheck and production build passed (174502 gzip bytes). All tests used local fixtures; physical MIDI hardware and the full show rehearsal remain part of later overall verification.

requirements.section: 0.9 Disconnect honesty on operator screens (UI review 1, 2, 3; live findings)
evidence: SongCueLoader disables loads while disconnected, starting or running; waits for echoed group confirmation before closing; retains selection on failure. Invalid or mismatched map formats are shown explicitly and blocked. Offset must be a finite, nonnegative whole frame count; buildSongAutomationEvents enforces the same boundary.

Hook includes requireStopped and expectedFormat preconditions. Real Worker tests prove that a load arriving after the clock starts or the format changes leaves the existing cue group intact. Component tests cover invalid/mismatched formats, negative offsets, failed saves, pending confirmation and running/offline guards.

Validation: full web suite passed (1202 unit tests, 94 Worker tests, migration/client boundaries); typecheck and production build passed (174502 gzip bytes). All tests used local fixtures; physical MIDI hardware and the full show rehearsal remain part of later overall verification.

requirements.section: 0.9 Disconnect honesty on operator screens (UI review 1, 2, 3; live findings)
evidence: Both clock displays and source controls derive running state from the same authoritative relay snapshot; local generator activation waits for a grant and running-state echo. TimecodeDisplay exposes matching accessible running/stopped/disconnected status.

A test renders the real useTimecode hook with both TimecodeDisplay sizes and TimecodeSourceSelector, and verifies stopped/Starting before confirmation, both clocks running plus Stop Generator after confirmation, and both disconnected with disabled transport after socket close.

Validation: full web suite passed (1202 unit tests, 94 Worker tests, migration/client boundaries); typecheck and production build passed (174502 gzip bytes). All tests used local fixtures; physical MIDI hardware and the full show rehearsal remain part of later overall verification.

request-database.server.ts scopes D1 sessions and Prisma clients to each Worker request or scheduled task. requirements.section: 1.5 Master only mutations, jump threshold, format change guard (audit H19, H18, H21, TC/M4)
evidence: TimecodeRelay now grants one socket control per show. Opening a viewer does not claim it; Take control or the first explicit edit/start reserves an available room synchronously. Every external mutation checks this owner after live session/permission validation. HTTP commands require the owning socket's authenticated user/session and cannot acquire control themselves. Internal Bridge feeds remain separately attested and do not acquire editing ownership.

Control resides in hibernating socket attachments and is released on disconnect or permission revocation. Existing generator ownership migrates on wake-up. A running local source must Stop before releasing control; delayed feeds cannot restart it or reclaim a released room. Editing ownership never suppresses a live Bridge feed.

Timecode and song editors show available/yours/other status with Take control and Release control. Rejected edits retain form drafts and fail immediately; control metadata does not cause false sequence gaps. Tests: timecode-control.worker.test.ts, useTimecode.test.tsx, and real two-tab smoke-timecode-control.mjs.

requirements.section: 1.5 Master only mutations, jump threshold, format change guard (audit H19, H18, H21, TC/M4)
evidence: TimecodeRelay disables the existing triggersEnabled gate on forward or backward jumps greater than two nominal seconds. Feed updates and explicit seeks are guarded, including fresh Bridge standby handover. Normal midnight rollover is continuous. Clock/display updates continue; fired flags are never reset by a jump.

The clock journal persists the hold reason and disabled gate before evaluation. Re-arm requires confirmation of the current server-generated hold ID; a newer jump invalidates an older confirmation. Re-arm starts from the current frame, skips missed cues, and does not startup-match an unchanged position after signal loss. Reset and Stop do not clear the review requirement.

Generation checks cancel queued scheduled work across jumps, disable, Stop, seek and signal loss, including when re-arm arrives before a slow predecessor acknowledges. Already-dispatched remote effects cannot be recalled. The UI shows the from/to positions and an explicit review/resume dialog; emergency Disable remains immediate.
